Subject: Question on hosted pricing: chat completions vs responses endpoints

Hi Marissa,

Quick one — our engineering team is trying to reconcile bill estimates for a pilot. We use a mix of multi-turn assistant flows (system + user + assistant turns) and some batched, single-response generation for product descriptions.

Can you confirm: on Redwood Hosted, are Chat Completions (the older /chat endpoints) metered differently than the Responses endpoint? Specifically:
- How are tokens counted for system messages, function call metadata, and streaming?
- Are input/output tokens billed separately or consolidated into a single "token unit"?
- Any special cases (e.g., tool/function responses, truncated responses, streaming partial tokens) we should watch for?

Would appreciate a concrete example mapping (payload -> billed units). Also, any baseline ratecard numbers for 1M input/output tokens to use in our cost model would help.

Thanks —
Oliver

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list of asks, this is a great place to start. Looping in Karthik (pricing) and Aditya (SE) to give a precise mapping and a baseline ratecard attachment.

Short answers up front:
- Metering approach: Responses (new unified endpoints) and Chat Completions both bill on token usage, but the mapping rules differ for historical/legacy endpoints. System messages and assistant messages are counted as input tokens when they are part of the request context; generated assistant output counts as output tokens.
- Input vs output: We report input and output tokens separately on invoices (so you can see both), and ratecard line items exist for each.
- Function calls/tool outputs: if the model emits a function call as text in the response payload, those tokens are billed as output. If your application synthesizes a tool response server-side (outside the model) and then you send it back as part of context, those are input tokens.

I'll attach a short mapping example and the baseline PDF. Karthik, can you confirm the two baseline line items (per 1k input tokens, per 1k output tokens) and any committed-discount tiers we should flag for a pilot->POC conversion?

Best,
Marissa

Oliver, Marissa — adding concrete numbers. Attaching a one-pager but pasting the essentials inline for quick modeling: 

Baseline list rates (Hosted API, public ratecard v3):
- Input tokens: $0.60 per 1k tokens (USD)
- Output tokens: $1.20 per 1k tokens (USD)
- Responses call overhead: no additional per-call surcharge on basic hosted plans; metering is token-based.

Examples (approx):
1) Multi-turn assistant request (legacy /chat example)
- Request payload includes: system (40 tokens), previous user turn (80 tokens), recent assistant turn (90 tokens), current user (35 tokens) => input tokens = 245
- Model generates assistant reply (output) = 180 tokens => output tokens = 180
- Billed units: 245 input tokens and 180 output tokens at the rates above

2) Single-shot generation via Responses endpoint with function calling (streaming)
- Request context (prompt + metadata) = 120 input tokens
- Model streams a function_call payload: emitted text representing function name and arguments = 60 output tokens; later your app calls a 3rd-party service and returns results as part of a follow-up request (those results count as input tokens when sent back)
- Billed: 120 input tokens, 60 output tokens. Partial streaming chunks are aggregated by the final token count — we bill on final token counts, not per-chunk.

Edge cases:
- Truncated responses: billed for tokens actually generated (if generation truncated by max_tokens param you pay for what was produced).
- System messages: always part of input if sent in the request.
- Stop sequences: do not change billing rules; generation stops when token decoder halts, and billing follows produced tokens.

Discounts/commits: pilot-level discounts are commonly given via a short-term usage commit (3–6 months) — typical initial discount tiers: 10% off list for $25k+/mo committed spend, 15% for $75k+/mo, gradational beyond. We can provide a tailored committed-rate schedule if you share expected monthly token mix (input vs output).

Marissa — attaching the baseline PDF and an example_payloads file with the JSON-encoded requests -> annotated billing counts. Aditya — anything to add on streaming/partial-chunk aggregation?

Thanks,

Oliver — quick technical clarifications from the SE side:
- Streaming: Redwood aggregates streaming pieces server-side; final token counters are what we report. If you read streamed tokens on your side, your own gauges may see slightly different rounding; use our billed counts for cost modeling.
- Functions: When the model emits a function_call object (name + args) those tokens are included in output billing. If you call the function and then send back the function result inside a new request, that new payload's tokens count as input.
- History trimming: when we trim context for very long histories, tokens removed from the request are not billed (because they were not sent). If you rely on deterministic billing between dev and prod, recommend sending explicit context windows or using our prefix caching feature to avoid variability.

One gotcha: legacy "chat" endpoints historically included a small per-request metadata surcharge for control-plane work on some older SKUs — this surcharge has been removed from the Responses public SKU; if you're mapping older invoices, we'll help reconcile chargebacks.

Happy to hop on a quick walkthrough with your infra team and show live billing for a sample conversation if that's helpful.
